title: LoKO: Low-Rank Kalman Optimizer for Online Fine-Tuning of Large Models

contributions.purpose: Provide a second-order alternative to gradient-based optimizers for online fine-tuning of large models, cast as an optimal filtering/state-estimation problem.
contributions.mechanism: LoKO: combine LoRA's low-rank decomposition with the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) so that only the small set of low-rank trainable parameters is estimated online, demonstrating LoRA-Kalman compatibility. Claimed to be the first successful attempt to fine-tune large transformers (millions of parameters) with a Kalman filter.
contributions.evaluation: Reported to converge with fewer iterations and yield better (or at least comparable) performance than commonly used optimizers with LoRA.
contributions.domain: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning / optimization for large models
contributions.source_quote: Based on the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) method, introduced by Hu et al.(2021), which significantly reduces the number of trainable parameters, we demonstrated its compatibility with the Kalman filter. Also, we showed that this combination offers faster performance than traditional optimizers in online fine-tuning scenarios.

contributions.purpose: Reduce the computational complexity of Kalman iterations and make observation-noise estimation robust.
contributions.mechanism: Diagonal approximation of the covariance matrix P (reducing complexity from quadratic to linear in trainable params) combined with an exponential moving average (EMA) to estimate the observation noise covariance R, integrated into the LoRA framework; also a Taylor-based refinement of R.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves improved performance without additional computational cost; results shown to have minimal sensitivity to covariance initialization (Fig. 7, CIFAR-100/ViT-B16).
contributions.domain: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning / optimization for large models
contributions.source_quote: We employ a diagonal approximation for the covariance matrix P, a common approach to reduce the computational overhead from quadratic to linear. By integrating this with the exponential moving average (EMA) for estimating the matrix R and incorporating it into the LoRA framework, we achieve improved performance without additional computational cost.

contributions.purpose: Empirically demonstrate LoKO's effectiveness for online fine-tuning across vision and language classification tasks.
contributions.mechanism: Online fine-tuning experiments across computer vision and language modeling benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet100, SST-2, COLA, MRPC; LoKO consistently achieves superiority over or at least comparability with commonly used optimizers.
contributions.domain: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning / optimization for large models
contributions.source_quote: We conduct various experiments to demonstrate LoKO's performance in online fine-tuning classification tasks across computer vision and language modeling domains.

self_declared_provenance.quote: In this paper, we leverage the low-rank decomposition technique from LoRA to reduce the number of trainable parameters in specific layers. We show that the EKF algorithm can be particularly useful for fine-tuning
Ollivier (2018) theoretically demonstrated that EKF is effectively equivalent to online natural gradient descent. This offers a new perspective on advanced optimization

notes: Reject paper. Comparable/tie signal is explicit: the paper repeatedly claims 'superiority over (or at least comparability with)' commonly used optimizers, i.e. sometimes only on par. Caveat: evaluation limited to classification tasks in CV and language; broader domains (e.g. RL) left to future work. Builds directly on LoRA (Hu et al. 2021) + classic EKF (Kalman & Bucy 1961).
